headline: MACC Chief Under Probe; the System Investigating Him Answers to Those Who Appointed Him
context: Bloomberg alleged MACC Chief Azam Baki colluded with businessmen. He sued it for RM100 million over a report on his shareholdings. A minister called for an RCI; three days later the PM deferred the decision until an AG-led probe ends.

changes.summary: Correction: Earlier editions named the minister who called for a royal commission and said he was overruled; the reports we rely on name no minister, and the prime minister deferred the decision. The MACC Act sets up three oversight bodies, not four; the RM277 billion estimate is now attributed to the MACC chief; an unsupported 3.4% of GDP figure and a UN review recommendation we could not confirm are removed.

cards.big: Malaysia's anticorruption chief is under investigation; the system investigating him answers to those who appointed him
cards.sub: Bloomberg alleged Azam Baki colluded with businessmen. He sued it for RM100M over a report on his shareholdings. The PM deferred an RCI until an AG-led probe ends.

cards.big: The MACC Act sets up three oversight bodies. None of them can criminally investigate the MACC chief.
cards.sub: He sits on the advisory board, whose other members are appointed on the PM's advice. MPs and senators examine MACC's annual report. The complaints committee covers only non-criminal misconduct.

cards.big: A minister publicly called for an RCI on 24 February. Three days later, the PM put the decision off until the probe into Azam ends.
cards.sub: Under the MACC Act 2009, the PM advises on who heads MACC. His Cabinet also decides whether an RCI goes ahead.

cards.big: MACC chief Azam Baki estimated in May 2024 that corruption cost Malaysia about RM277 billion over five years.
cards.sub: CPI improved to 54th before the Bloomberg revelations. The RM100M suit signals investigating corruption carries a price.

cards.big: The question is not whether Azam Baki is guilty. It is whether any institution can answer that independently when every government has chosen not to build one.
The fix is a permanent independent oversight body for MACC. But that requires a government to surrender power over its own watchdog. None has.
